title: Lusin's theorem (compact form) for measurable maps from ℝ^P into a second-countable space
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, and let Y be a second-countable topological space with a σ-algebra in which every open set is measurable. Let μ be any measure on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Borel σ-algebra), let A ⊆ ℝ^P be a measurable set with μ(A) < ∞, let g : ℝ^P → Y be measurable, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞] be an extended nonnegative real with ε ≠ 0. Then there is a compact set K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε such that g is continuous on K (ContinuousOn g K).
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Y) (ε : ℝ≥0∞), Measurable g → MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → ε ≠ 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < ε ∧ ContinuousOn g K
